Poodle retrieving a duck

Poodles were originally bred for [waterfowl hunting](/wiki/Waterfowl_hunting "Waterfowl hunting").[[18]](#cite_note-FCI_Standard-18) Despite this history, they are currently classified as companion dogs by the FCI.[[18]](#cite_note-FCI_Standard-18) Since the late 1980s, some breeders in the United States and Canada have been selecting for dogs with drive for birds in order to revive the breed for hunting, with some success.[[39]](#cite_note-39) Poodles are highly trainable dogs that typically excel in obedience training.[[22]](#cite_note-AKCInfo-22) Historically, they were a popular circus dog. In addition to hunt tests, they do well in [agility](/wiki/Dog_agility "Dog agility") and rally.[[11]](#cite_note-Flaim-11) They are among the most popular service dog breeds.[[40]](#cite_note-40)

Poodles have been used as working dogs in the military since at least the 17th century, most likely because of their highly intelligent, trainable nature. Their background as a hunting dog makes them suitable to battlefields, and they can be trained to ignore gunfire. During the [English Civil War](/wiki/English_Civil_War "English Civil War"), [Prince Rupert of the Rhine](/wiki/Prince_Rupert_of_the_Rhine "Prince Rupert of the Rhine") had a famous [hunting Poodle](/wiki/Boy_(dog) "Boy (dog)") who would ride into battle with his master on horseback. [Napoleon Bonaparte](/wiki/Napoleon_Bonaparte "Napoleon Bonaparte") wrote in his memoirs about the faithfulness of a grenadier's pet Poodle who stayed with the body of his master at the [Battle of Marengo](/wiki/Battle_of_Marengo "Battle of Marengo").[[41]](#cite_note-41)

The office of deputy prime minister is the second highest position in the [Cabinet of Singapore](/wiki/Cabinet_of_Singapore "Cabinet of Singapore"), typically held by senior ministers. At times, two individuals could serve simultaneously as deputy prime ministers. The officeholder is generally assigned specific duties by the prime minister, including deputising in the [Parliament of Singapore](/wiki/Parliament_of_Singapore "Parliament of Singapore"). Additionally, the deputy prime minister often acts as prime minister during periods when the latter is abroad, on leave or incapacitated.

Established in [1959](/wiki/1959_Singaporean_general_election "1959 Singaporean general election") with Singapore's attainment of [self-governance](/wiki/Self-governance_of_Singapore "Self-governance of Singapore") from the [British Empire](/wiki/British_Empire "British Empire"), the first deputy prime minister was appointed by [Yang di-Pertuan Negara](/wiki/Yang_di-Pertuan_Negara "Yang di-Pertuan Negara") [William Goode](/wiki/William_Goode_(colonial_administrator) "William Goode (colonial administrator)"). The position retained its title following Singapore's merger with the [Federation of Malaya](/wiki/Federation_of_Malaya "Federation of Malaya"), [Sarawak](/wiki/Crown_Colony_of_Sarawak "Crown Colony of Sarawak") and [North Borneo](/wiki/Crown_Colony_of_North_Borneo "Crown Colony of North Borneo") to form [Malaysia](/wiki/Malaysia "Malaysia"), during which Singapore functioned as a [autonomous federated state](/wiki/State_of_Singapore_(Malaysia) "State of Singapore (Malaysia)") between 1963 and 1965. [Toh Chin Chye](/wiki/Toh_Chin_Chye "Toh Chin Chye") was the inaugural officeholder, serving from 1959 to 1968.[[1]](#cite_note-2) It was vacant from 1968 to 1973, when prime minister [Lee Kuan Yew](/wiki/Lee_Kuan_Yew "Lee Kuan Yew") did not pick a deputy for his [Third Cabinet](/wiki/Third_Lee_Kuan_Yew_Cabinet "Third Lee Kuan Yew Cabinet") after winning the [1968 Singaporean general election](/wiki/1968_Singaporean_general_election "1968 Singaporean general election").

The Taj Mahal was commissioned by [Shah Jahan](/wiki/Shah_Jahan "Shah Jahan") in 1631, to be built in the memory of his wife [Mumtaz Mahal](/wiki/Mumtaz_Mahal "Mumtaz Mahal"), who died on 17 June that year while giving birth to their 14th child, [Gauhara Begum](/wiki/Gauhara_Begum "Gauhara Begum").[[13]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAsher1992210-13)[[14]](#cite_note-14) Construction started in 1632, and the mausoleum was completed in 1648, while the surrounding buildings and garden were finished five years later.[[15]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESarkar191930,_31-15)[[16]](#cite_note-Creation_History-16)

The imperial court documenting Shah Jahan's grief after the death of Mumtaz Mahal illustrates the love story held as the inspiration for the Taj Mahal.[[17]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChaghtai193846-17) According to contemporary historians Muhammad Amin Qazvini, [Abdul Hamid Lahori](/wiki/Abdul_Hamid_Lahori "Abdul Hamid Lahori") and [Muhammad Saleh Kamboh](/wiki/Muhammad_Saleh_Kamboh "Muhammad Saleh Kamboh"), Shah Jahan did not show the same level of affection for others as he had shown Mumtaz while she was alive. After her death, he avoided royal affairs for a week due to his grief and gave up listening to music and lavish dressing for two years. Shah Jahan was enamoured by the beauty of the land at the south side of [Agra](/wiki/Agra "Agra") on which a mansion belonging to Raja [Jai Singh I](/wiki/Jai_Singh_I "Jai Singh I") stood. He chose the place for the construction of Mumtaz's tomb after which Jai Singh agreed to give it to emperor [Shah Jahan](/wiki/Shah_Jahan "Shah Jahan") in exchange for a large palace in the centre of Agra.[[18]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChaghtai193854-18)[[19]

As of 2014, Instagram's users are divided equally, with 50% iPhone owners and 50% Android owners. While Instagram has a neutral gender-bias format, 68% of Instagram users are female and 32% are male. Instagram's geographical use is shown to favor urban areas, as 17% of U.S. adults who live in urban areas use Instagram, while only 11% of adults in suburban and rural areas do so. While Instagram may appear to be one of the most widely used sites for photo sharing, only 7% of daily photo uploads, among the top four photo-sharing platforms, come from Instagram. Instagram has been proven to attract the younger generation, with 90% of its 150 million users under the age of 35. From June 2012 to June 2013, Instagram approximately doubled their number of users. With regards to income, 15% of U.S. Internet users who make less than $30,000 per year use Instagram, while 14% of those making $30,000 to $50,000 and 12% of users who make more than $50,000 per year do so.[[415]](#cite_note-416) With respect to the education demographic, respondents with some college education proved to be the most active on Instagram, with 23%. Following behind, college graduates consist of 18% and users with a high school diploma or less make up 15%. Among these Instagram users, 24% say they use the app several times a day.[[416]](#cite_note-417)

Smith") at Bell Labs in 1969,[[7]](#cite_note-7) based on [MOS capacitor](/wiki/MOS_capacitor "MOS capacitor") technology.[[8]](#cite_note-Williams-8) The [NMOS](/wiki/NMOS_logic "NMOS logic") [active-pixel sensor](/wiki/Active-pixel_sensor "Active-pixel sensor") was later invented by Tsutomu Nakamura's team at [Olympus](/wiki/Olympus_Corporation "Olympus Corporation") in 1985,[[9]](#cite_note-9)[[10]](#cite_note-fossum93-10)[[11]](#cite_note-11) which led to the development of the [CMOS](/wiki/CMOS "CMOS") active-pixel sensor (CMOS sensor) at the [NASA](/wiki/NASA "NASA") [Jet Propulsion Laboratory](/wiki/Jet_Propulsion_Laboratory "Jet Propulsion Laboratory") in 1993.[[12]](#cite_note-Fossum2014-12)[[10]](#cite_note-fossum93-10)

In the 1960s, [Eugene F. Lally](/wiki/Eugene_F._Lally "Eugene F. Lally") of the Jet Propulsion Laboratory was thinking about how to use a mosaic photo sensor to capture digital images.
